title: Clear conditions
summary: Simplify boolean expressions and flatten nested ifs with guard clauses.

steps.title: Say it once, say it plainly
body: Conditions grow clutter. A few rewrites are always safe, in any language:
| `if (x > 0) return true; else return false;` | `return x > 0;` |
A comparison already **is** a boolean. Wrapping it in `if ... return true else return false` adds four lines that say nothing.

steps.prompt: Match each cluttered condition to its plain form.
Which is equivalent to this function body for every input?

steps.title: Guard clauses
body: Nested ifs push the real work to the right and make you hold every condition in your head:
A **guard clause** handles each bad case first and leaves early. What remains is the happy path, flat and readable:
Each guard is the De Morgan negation of one nested condition. Every language with an early `return` supports this style.

steps.prompt: Each `return` leaves the function immediately. What is printed?
steps.explain: Because each guard returns, later checks can assume the earlier ones failed: by the `>= 50` line, `score` is known to be valid and under 90.

steps.prompt: Order the guards so `Ticket(10, false)` returns `"child"`, `Ticket(30, true)` returns `"member"` and `Ticket(30, false)` returns `"adult"`. Members of any age get the member price, so check that first.

steps.title: Flatten it
prompt: `CanVote` works but is nested three deep. Rewrite it with guard clauses: no `else`, and no `if` inside another `if`.
Rules: `age` under 18 gives `"too young"`, not registered gives `"not registered"`, already voted gives `"already voted"`, otherwise `"ok"`.
starter: string CanVote(int age, bool registered, bool voted)
solution: string CanVote(int age, bool registered, bool voted)
template: Dojo.Eq("CanVote(17, true, false)", "too young", CanVote(17, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(30, false, false)", "not registered", CanVote(30, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(30, true, true)", "already voted", CanVote(30, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("CanVote(18, true, false)", "ok", CanVote(18, true, false));
hints: Negate each outer condition and return its failure message straight away.
`if (age < 18) return "too young";` is the first guard.

steps.title: Simplify the shipping rule
prompt: Write `bool FreeShipping(double total, bool isMember, bool isExpress)` as a single `return` of one clear expression.
Shipping is free when the order is **not** express **and** either the total is at least 50 or the customer is a member.
solution: bool FreeShipping(double total, bool isMember, bool isExpress)
template: Dojo.Eq("60, not member, standard: free", true, FreeShipping(60, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("20, member, standard: free", true, FreeShipping(20, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("20, not member, standard: paid", false, FreeShipping(20, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("60, member, express: paid", false, FreeShipping(60, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("50 exactly counts", true, FreeShipping(50, false, false));

forbid.message: Does not compare booleans to true or false

hints: The "either" part needs parentheses, because `&&` binds tighter than `||`.
